chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Wahb ibn Hafth from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who partners with another man regarding a commodity and appoints him as manager over it. He said: 'If there is profit, it belongs to him (the manager), and if there is a loss (deficit), it is upon him.'

And I asked him about a slave who buys and sells, and his master has knowledge of this until the debt accumulates to equal its price (or the value of the slave). He said: 'Ease is sought for him regarding what is upon him (in debt repayment).'
ai.seo_question: What are the financial responsibilities and liabilities of a business partner or manager in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the risk-sharing mechanism in *Mudarabah*-style partnerships, establishing that the manager bears the financial burden of loss while retaining profit, a principle foundational to Shia commercial jurisprudence. It further illustrates the juristic flexibility (*istis'a*) granted to a *mudabbir* slave who accumulates debt through authorized trade, reflecting the Shia emphasis on equitable debt relief and practical commercial ease.
